title: Bunk's 'low gravy'
summary: Bunk answered praise for the quiet playing by saying they had the band in the low gravy; they note the record does not capture it.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Did Bunk ever discuss with you at all about playing the last chorus louder, or coming down real soft before the last chorus, or anything like that?

Well he did mention about the same night, you know, like, I guess it was me or somebody else and myself, we went up to Bunk and said, man, you know, like, this playing real quiet, this is really terrific, you know, and he said, yeah, well we really got the band getting some low gravy, he called it low gravy, which I had never heard of before.
Oh yeah, I believe Harold or Stoney or somebody told me that, it must have been that same night, yeah, he said, yeah, we got him dipping down into the low gravy tonight, as if it's
really good. Yeah, he kind of, well sometimes Bunk wouldn't acknowledge, you know, something that you might say about the band on a particular night, you know, he just kind of.
Yeah, act like he didn't hear you.
Yeah, yeah, but this particular time he did, he answered us right to the point, you know.
Yeah, that's the low gravy. That was wonderful. That's the jelly roll title and low gravy.
Yeah, well of course the funny thing is that record doesn't sound, doesn't do the low gravy thing at all.
